question: does MATH 237 discrete math count toward the computer science major or is it only for math majors
answer:
Yes. In the Computer Science BS (Bachelor of Science), the major requires “MATH 205 MATHEMATICAL STRUCTURES or MATH 237 DISCRETE STRUCTURES” [1]. The recommended plan for students admitted during 2026–2027 also lists MATH 237 or MATH 205 in the second-year fall semester [1]. It is not only for math majors: the Mathematics BS also accepts MATH 237 or MATH 205 as a required course in both its Traditional and Teacher Education tracks [2]. MATH 237 is 4 credits. Its prerequisites are CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S and MATH 121; courses may be taken concurrently with MATH 237 [3].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-CMPS) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-MATH) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/MATH237)

question: what does data structures cover and how many credits is it
answer:
CMPS 231 Data Structures is 4 credits. It studies basic data structures and related algorithms, including stacks, queues, deques, arrays, linked lists, trees, graphs, strings, sorting, searching, and file structures. A course fee is required. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CMPS231)

question: Is there a data science major or minor at Ramapo? I'm a CS major thinking about adding one
answer:
Yes—Ramapo lists a Data Science BS (Bachelor of Science) and a Data Science Minor [1][2]. The catalog minor requires CMPS 130, CMPS 240, DATA 101, DATA 301, and one elective from BADM 225, BIOL 354, MATH 353, MATH 370, POLI 316, PSYC 242, SOCI 308, or SWRK 307 [2]. Also published: Data Science 4+1 and Data Science MS [2].

To add a minor, the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) says to complete the online major/minor declaration form: https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/declare-major-minor-certificate/. The Registrar’s Office will update your record in 5–7 days after submission [13]. Contact the Center for Student Success at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441 [13].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-DSCI) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-MN-DSCI) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/)

question: Can I use a CMPS course to satisfy a gen ed requirement or do CS courses not count for gen ed at all?
answer:
Yes. The catalog lists CMPS 110 MODERN COMPUTER LITERACY: WEB, SECURITY AND AI and CMPS 147 COMPUTER SCIENCE I as Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR), so CS courses do count; those courses satisfy Quantitative Reasoning. [4] Not every CMPS course necessarily does: check the approved General Education course list in the College Catalog. [5]

question: should i take operating systems or software engineering next semester, which one is easier
answer:
I don’t have verified information about which course is easier or which you should take; the pages provided don’t describe Software Engineering. CMPS 311 Operating Systems is 4 credits, has a required course fee, and is writing intensive. It covers operating-system design, use and analysis, including computer architecture, memory, processes, information, device control, structure and evaluation. Its prerequisites include CMPS 220, CMPS 231 (minimum grade C), CRWT 102 or CRWT 102S, and either MATH 205 or MATH 237. [1]
